PADLAB GUIDE · NINTENDO

Nintendo Switch Pro Controller Test Online

By PadLab · Updated October 9, 2026

A Switch Pro Controller can appear differently depending on the browser, operating system and connection mode. PadLab helps you see the inputs actually available to the page.

Start controller test →

Connect and test a Switch Pro Controller

  1. Pair the controller or connect with a USB data cable.
  2. Open the PadLab tester and press a button.
  3. Press face buttons, D-pad, Plus, Minus, Home, Capture, shoulders and stick clicks.
  4. Move both sticks through their range, release them, and run a drift sample.

Why the letters may look unfamiliar

Nintendo’s printed button letters use a different physical arrangement from Xbox labels. A browser standard mapping describes control positions, while an unmapped device may expose only numbers. PadLab avoids relabeling unknown inputs.

Check Switch Pro stick drift

Run the drift sample with both sticks untouched. Compare mean and peak radial offset with the deadzone configured in your game. The visual deadzone slider never changes raw values or controller settings.

See the stick drift guide.

USB and Bluetooth checks

A USB cable must carry data. For Bluetooth, confirm the controller is paired to the computer and not claimed by a console. If it appears without a standard mapping, detection works; only label assignment is missing.

Separate printed letters from input positions

PadLab’s standard diagram uses Xbox-style position labels. Nintendo’s face-button letters occupy different positions. Press the bottom, right, left and top physical buttons separately and compare their input cells; a different letter on the diagram is not evidence of a failed button.

When no standard mapping is provided, use the numbered input list. Do not assume that the first two axes are the left stick on an unmapped device.

Check shoulder inputs without expecting analog travel

The Switch Pro Controller’s ZL and ZR controls are digital. A two-state value is expected for those physical controls; they should not be judged against the gradual travel of an Xbox or DualSense analog trigger. Check press and release for L, R, ZL and ZR individually.

Compare connection behavior

CheckWhat to record
USBWhether the operating system and browser see a device using a data cable.
BluetoothWhether pairing completes and a physical button exposes inputs to the page.
MappingWhether the browser supplies standard positions or only raw numbers.
Extra controlsWhether Home or Capture is exposed independently in this environment.

A controller working on a Nintendo console does not establish that every feature is accessible in a computer browser. Follow the detection checklist when no values appear and the button guide when only one input seems missing.
